You are evaluating a source-code privacy technique. Your job is to defeat it. A tool called `effigy` takes a source file from some **original problem domain** and rewrites or obscures it so the file can be sent to a third-party model for architectural review without revealing what the original code was about. You are that third party, and you are hostile. You have **complete knowledge of the tool**. It is a public research repository: its algorithms, its configuration, and its prompts are all published. Assume nothing is secret except the original source itself. Specifically: The artifact is the original source file with **every trace of the author's chosen vocabulary mechanically removed, and its shape left exactly intact.** Specifically, by a deterministic program with no model in the loop: - Every identifier the author named — types, functions, methods, fields, parameters, variables, constants, packages — is replaced by `ident_NNNN` or `Ident_NNNN`, numbered in order of first appearance. Capitalisation is preserved, because in Go it carries exportedness and in JSX it distinguishes a component from a DOM element. - Every string literal, template literal, regular-expression literal and JSX text node is replaced by `str_NNNN`. Character/rune literals are replaced by distinct placeholder characters, so a `switch` over three of them still has three distinguishable cases. - Every comment is blanked to `// -`, occupying the same lines it did before, so comment position and density survive but no comment text does. - Imports of the file's **own** module are renamed; imports of the standard library and of third-party packages are left verbatim, along with the members selected on them (`slog.Logger`, `sql.Open`, `http.StatusOK`, `useState`). HTML element and attribute names are also left verbatim where they appear on a plain DOM element. - Numeric literals are left unchanged. What is therefore fully preserved: control flow, call graph, function and method arity, nesting depth, coupling between files, the standard-library and framework API surface actually used, the number and position of every declaration, and the line count.
